open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a single finite rule system \(\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}\), independent of \(D,K\), whose typed local rules are sound on the full Dai compatibility class and prove the simultaneous extension statement: every endpoint left circular by its closure admits tail and arrowhead witnesses in \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) that preserve every fixed closure mark across the indicator-free observational projection and all indicator-bearing nonobservational projections.
open_obligations.obstruction: The established certificate theorems provide endpointwise opposing witnesses by a global enumeration over basal DAGs, ancestor-closed selected sets, and normalized targets.  They do not imply that invariant marks admit a bounded local derivation, nor that ordinary single-MAG or no-selection completion moves can be coupled through one basal DAG, one selected set, and one ordered unknown-target family for arbitrarily many regimes.  In particular, no frozen lemma proves that a completion chosen to flip one residual endpoint preserves all already fixed marks and remains simultaneously realizable in every twin projection.  Finite per-instance enumeration cannot by itself be compacted into finitely many rule templates independent of \(D,K\).
open_obligations.attempted: The ordinary within-regime FCI route closes discriminating-path consequences but supplies only regimewise MAG completions.  The Jaber unknown-target intervention route omits pre-treatment selection, and the Zhang circle-component route treats one MAG equivalence class.  Combining those routes with Dai descendant and ancestral-selection labels establishes sound candidate consequences but leaves the common-basal paired-extension step unproved.  A second route tried to extract local rules from the exact target-residual enumerator; it fails because the acceptance predicate uses global acyclicity, ancestor closure, descendant closure, and simultaneous regime matching, with no proved bounded-obstruction or finite-basis theorem.
